title: get_status.changed_files mangles renamed files into a single 'old -> new' string
description: When a file has been renamed, `git status --porcelain` emits a single line of the form `R  old.py -> new.py` (status code 'R', two-char status + space, then 'old -> new'). The parser does `line[3:].strip().strip('"')`, which yields the literal string `old.py -> new.py` as ONE entry in `changed_files`, instead of the new path `new.py`. Consequently the status panel shows a nonsensical pseudo-filename for every rename, and any consumer treating entries as real paths (e.g. opening the file) breaks. The same line[3:] slice also fails to C-unescape git's quoted paths (git emits `"my file.py"` / backslash-escaped octal for non-ASCII and special chars); `.strip('"')` removes only the outer quotes and leaves embedded escapes intact. Note save_progress/_auto_commit are unaffected because they parse `git diff --cached --name-only`, which prints each path on its own line with no arrow form — only get_status uses the porcelain arrow format.
evidence: Reproduced: `git mv a.py b.py; git status --porcelain` -> `R  a.py -> b.py`. With this single line, the loop appends `('R  a.py -> b.py')[3:]` = `'a.py -> b.py'` (after strip) to changed_files. Expected entry is `b.py`. No test in tests/test_git.py exercises a rename, so this is uncovered.
